reason: Version 1's clearances, which hold for every town: a person arrives with two metres between their standing point and the occupied plan extent of a street-furniture item or tree, and two metres from every residential node under the town routine. This version is pinned only by a town on land whose land holds a sea, so the sea the person's words or setting named is in their first view, with the town. Such a town's arrival is a seafront view: the clear spot on the seaward footway of the street nearest the sea that runs along the shore, facing across the street to the land side's fronts, mid-block: the spot nearest the town's centre, which stands in a block's middle because the city grammar lays a block centred on the town's centre (measured on both presets for every block length the schema admits, 90 to 140 m: the arrival stands 0.48 to 0.52 of the way along its block). From there the fronts across the street stand about 9 to 12 m off and nothing of the town stands behind, so the view along the shore shows several fronts at a readable angle; the land side's own footway puts a person within a metre of the wall beside them, which a view along the street sees at a grazing angle. A spot is on the seaward footway of a street along the shore when the way it faces across the street (toward the street's crown) points away from the sea and lies no more than 45 degrees from the way inland: shore_street_most_permille is the tangent of that angle in thousandths. The street nearest the sea is the one whose crown lies farthest toward it. The page's first view then looks along the street, the fronts on the land side and open water on the seaward side (town-first-view version 5). Where no clear spot lies on such a footway, the spot nearest the town's centre is taken, as version 1 takes it, so the town's own first view stands. Every other town, and every town made before this version, keeps version 1.
